text: The shipped game must be functional, clear, communicative of what is happening, and technically performant, because these are the stated inspection axes.
Ship no jackpot, no gamble/double-up, no continuation of a prior round, and no early cashout control.
The disclaimer must convey that a malfunction voids all wins and plays.
The disclaimer must convey that a consistent internet connection is required.
The disclaimer must tell the player to reload the game after a disconnection to finish incomplete rounds.
The disclaimer must convey that expected return is a long-run figure.
The disclaimer must convey that the display is illustrative and models no physical machine.
The disclaimer must convey that the RGS response, not the frontend, settles winnings.

Present in the platform's template disclaimer as its closing line. Whether this line is itself mandatory, or is merely part of the template a studio may replace with its own wording under R1-19, is UNKNOWN from this page; note also that it sits against the project's own no-Stake-branding rule and should be ruled on rather than assumed.
In social mode, never render "currency"; use "token".
Make the max win figure printed in the game rules equal the maths package max win, per mode.
Never submit a bet above 500,000 USD, so the bet ladder and any buy cost must stay at or under that ceiling or the round errors with 400.
2-star rating only: the build must show considerable creativity or originality plus strong development quality, with polish allowed to trail established studios.
Provide enough gameplay depth that a player keeps betting past the first spin or two; shallow depth is a named cause of a 1-star or lower rating.
Every shipped audio and visual asset must be original to this title, with no web-sdk sample-game backgrounds, symbols or animations remaining anywhere in the bundle.
Show the live balance in the normal-play UI, updating with wagers and wins.
Any round with a payout above zero must present its final win amount legibly.
Autoplay must sit behind an explicit confirmation step, so a single click can never start a run of consecutive bets.
Observed play, including paid combinations, must match the published rules and paytable exactly.
Parse replay query parameters at boot and enter a replay mode that loads the identified round, honouring currency, language, social mode and bet size parameters.
Replay must load and play with no session and no authorisation, so a shared public URL works for a viewer who is not logged in.
Read and use all six required query parameters: replay, game, version, mode, event, rgs_url.
Build the replay request as a GET on exactly that path shape, with rgs_url taken from the query parameter and the four path segments in that order.
Fetch the round data on load, with no click or input needed to start loading.
Issue the replay fetch using the values taken from the query string, not defaults or hardcoded values.
A visible loading indicator covers the fetch window.
Replay makes no authenticate, play, end-round or wallet calls; only the public replay endpoint is touched.
A user-facing error state when the replay fetch fails, rather than a blank screen or a silent hang.
No control or path anywhere in replay mode can begin a real-money session.

Ship only static assets; zero runtime requests to any external host, including external font, CDN, analytics or image hosts. The same line names external font downloads as the common failure and notes they log console errors.

The table at lines 51 to 100 is the display specification for every supported currency: for each currency code the game must render the platform's exact display token, on the platform's side of the amount (prefix for USD, CAD, JPY and most others; suffix for DKK, PLN, VND, CLP, ARS, SAR, ILS, AED, TND, OMR, QAR, XGC, XSC, XEC), matching the Example column. Header row, upstream tabs rendered as single spaces.
Keep currency out of round logic, bet arithmetic and outcome selection; it may change only formatting.
Clamp every wager the game can submit to the authenticated minBet and maxBet, not to a hardcoded ladder.
Offer bet levels starting at $0.01, $0.02, $0.05 and $0.10 rather than a $0.10 floor.
Determine the game's minimum win multiplier and render win amounts with 3 decimal places if it is >= 0.1x, 4 if it is below.
Show the extra decimal places only while the base bet is under $0.10; above that, use normal currency precision.
In-game win readouts must show the exact win amount with no rounding; the balance readout may stay at 2 decimal places.
A Vite-built frontend must set base to "./" so the bundle resolves its assets relative to the hosted game path.

The client must play back the round's bookEvents strictly in the order the book supplies them, resolving each one before starting the next, so no later event (for example a win presentation) is shown ahead of an earlier one (for example the spin or reveal).
The game's runtime behaviour must match the documentation handed to Carrot, so the docs and the build cannot diverge.
No Prohibited Content anywhere in the game, including references to it; see R9-06 for the definition that binds this.
Audit every shipped string, symbol, sound and marketing asset against these four categories, including third-party IP infringement.
Run and record a security pass over the shipped bundle and its dependencies, and remove what it finds.
What the player sees on the reels, in win presentation and on the paytable must be the same event the maths package emitted, with no drift between the two.
The submitted title must be materially distinct from anything already uploaded, not a reskin; also blocks submitting a second near-identical build of our own.
Nothing in the shipped game may embarrass Carrot or Stake; this is the clause a machine-generated-looking string, a placeholder or an off-brand asset would be judged under.
Prove no GPL or other copyleft dependency is bundled into, compiled with or linked to the shipped build, and that every third-party licence in the tree is complied with.
The shipped game must not collect, store or transmit player personal data to us: no studio-side analytics, telemetry or logging endpoint carrying player data.

The submitted game must be original, guideline-compliant, non-infringing and free of unlawful, offensive or defamatory content; the competition rules re-impose the terms' content standard as an entry condition.
Name the exact frontend build and maths version in the approval request, and expect approval to bind to that pair only.
Write and submit a short theme-and-mechanics blurb alongside the approval request.
Submit only a finished build; work-in-progress submissions are out of order.
Clear every requirement before submitting; a partial submission is held rather than reviewed.
The build must average at least 1 star over three independent reviewers across design, gameplay and maths compliance, or it is rejected.
Treat the two size caps as publish-time blockers, so the size check happens before upload rather than after a failed publish.
Report the count of non-zero weight payouts as part of the submitted maths evidence.
Background plus foreground must total 3MB or less as a pair; the provider logo is not named in this cap.
Foreground is delivered as a high resolution PNG with a genuine alpha channel; JPG is not permitted for this asset.
Name the foreground file `<GameTitle>-FG.png`.
Supply the studio's official provider logo, not the game logo or a wordmark variant.
Provider logo is delivered as a high resolution PNG with a genuine alpha channel (same clause as R4-20 but stated for the logo asset).
Name the logo file `<ProviderName>-Logo.png`, provider name first, `-Logo` suffix.
The provider logo must stay readable when scaled down to tile size, so thin strokes and small type in the logo are a defect.

Tile pixel geometry is NOT stated anywhere in this capture: no pixel dimensions, no aspect ratio, no minimum resolution number, no safe area, no colour space. The only size-adjacent clauses are "High resolution" (lines 32, 36, 40) and the 3MB combined cap (line 28). Any specific tile geometry figure must come from another source, not from this page.
At submission, upload the contents of dist/ (not the folder itself) into the platform's frontend files slot.
Written notification to Carrot the moment we detect a defect, including ones we find ourselves after submission.
Submission is an upload to the platform for assessment against criteria Carrot sets and can change.
Do not treat an upload, a passing gate or a portal state as acceptance; only Carrot's written notice is acceptance.
Deliver object code within 3 days of acceptance, and any updated object code within 10 days of finishing a modification or new version.
Produce and hand over integration, operation and ongoing-management documentation; this is the same Game Documentation the artefact must conform to under R9-03 and R9-12.
Every test obligation in the agreement is a cross-OS and cross-browser matrix, not a single-browser run.
Complete identity and verification document submission, otherwise no fee is payable however well the game performs.
Grant Carrot continuous real-time access to the development environment, which in practice means the repository and build environment must be presentable at any moment.
Fund and supply whatever the certification and jurisdictional-approval process asks for, where the requirement stems from our own design.
On any notified breach of the clause 7.1a) game standards, remediate immediately at our cost; failure to satisfy Carrot leads to deactivation and licence termination under 7.1c).

At registration the studio must supply these six items, including an explicit 18-or-over confirmation and a declaration of individual-developer or authorised-company-representative status, plus a link to the GitHub repository.
Three entry steps, all completed before the Closing Date: hold an account, build the game on the platform, and submit it through the platform's own submission process.
Hard submission deadline for competition eligibility, 11:59pm AEDT 1 August 2026; entries after it are not considered, and the Promoter may move the date by publishing an update.
Register exactly one payout wallet on the team settings page; without it no payout can be made.
